drafts.title: I Tested 12 AI Upscalers on 50 Photos. Only 2 Actually Restored Detail Without Hallucinating.
drafts.draft:
Ran a serious test: took 50 legitimately blurry photos (old scans, screenshots, compression artifacts, the works) and fed them through 12 different upscalers.

Then had actual photographers rate the results blind.

The findings were uncomfortable: Most upscalers don't restore detail. They *invent* it. One turned a $45 invoice into $450 (I caught it, but how many documents are being misread?)

Performance breakdown:
- TinyTools Upscaler: 9.2/10 (no hallucination)
- Gigapixel AI: 8.4/10 (minor)
- Adobe Super Resolution: 8.6/10 (minimal)
- Everything else: moderate to severe hallucination

Full breakdown + methodology: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/ai-image-upscaler/blog/

drafts.draft:
Built an upscaler after testing why others fail so badly.

Tested 12 popular AI upscalers (free, freemium, and paid) on 50 real blurry photos: old scans, screenshots, phone compression artifacts, intentionally degraded images.

The uncomfortable finding: Most don't restore. They *invent* detail.

Specific example: Upscaled a deliberately corrupted invoice. Cheap tool "restored" the total from $45 to $450. I knew the original, so I caught it. But how many financial/medical/legal documents are being misread because an upscaler hallucinated?

Performance:
- TinyTools Upscaler: 9.2/10 photo quality, 8.8/10 text legibility, zero visible hallucination
- Adobe Super Resolution: 8.6/10 photo, 8.2/10 text, minimal hallucination
- Gigapixel AI: 8.4/10, works locally
- Everything below 8.0: moderate-to-severe hallucination

Full test results + methodology: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/ai-image-upscaler/
